review_notes: I read the whole file and the simp-tagged lemmas in the neighbouring BimoduleTensor files, mainly Basic.lean. I also checked the Mathlib simp lemmas about whiskering and tensorHom. I did not run Lean, so the finding is a static analysis of rule overlap and not an observed simp failure. I did not assess whether the `let _ := bimoduleMonoidalCategory Γ; lhs = rhs` statement shape lets simp match the instance. Only the whiskering overlap is reported.

findings.excerpt: M ◁ f = bimoduleTensorMap Γ Γ Γ (𝟙 M) f := (rfl)
findings.problem: Mathlib's monoidal simp set treats `◁` and `▷` as the normal form. `whiskerLeft_comp` and `comp_whiskerRight` are simp lemmas that split `M ◁ (f ≫ g)` and `(f ≫ g) ▷ P`, and `id_tensorHom`/`tensorHom_id` turn `𝟙 X ⊗ₘ f` into `X ◁ f`. These two lemmas are also simp, and they rewrite every whisker into `bimoduleTensorMap (𝟙 M) f` or `bimoduleTensorMap f (𝟙 P)`. On `M ◁ (f ≫ g)` both rules match at the root. If this file's rule fires first, the result is `bimoduleTensorMap Γ Γ Γ (𝟙 M) (f ≫ g)`. The local simp lemma `bimoduleTensorMap_comp` only matches when both arguments are composites, `(f ≫ f') (g ≫ g')`, and `𝟙 M` is not one, so it cannot split this term. If Mathlib's rule fires first, the result is `M ◁ f ≫ M ◁ g`, which then expands to `bimoduleTensorMap (𝟙 M) f ≫ bimoduleTensorMap (𝟙 M) g`. So the two competing rules can give different normal forms, and the expansion also removes the generic whiskering lemmas (`whisker_exchange`, `whiskerLeft_id`, and so on) from the simp set. I did not run Lean to confirm which rule fires first.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `bimoduleMonoidalCategory_whiskerLeft` and `bimoduleMonoidalCategory_whiskerRight`, so that `◁` and `▷` stay the simp normal form, as Mathlib has it. Keep the two `rfl` lemmas for `simp only`/`rw`. Keep `bimoduleMonoidalCategory_tensorHom` as simp. Alternatively, keep the expansion but add simp lemmas `bimoduleTensorMap (𝟙 M) (f ≫ g) = bimoduleTensorMap (𝟙 M) f ≫ bimoduleTensorMap (𝟙 M) g` and the right-hand analogue, so both routes reach the same form.
findings.benefit: Composites of whiskered morphisms get one normal form that the generic monoidal simp lemmas keep working on. Downstream proofs about `M ◁ (f ≫ g)` no longer risk getting stuck on an unsplit `bimoduleTensorMap (𝟙 M) (f ≫ g)`.
